author: Haiku critic
text: The discard-all control has three different descriptions. The inventory puts an undo clear icon on the Application and Reset SectionHeaders, with a title that says it discards changes since the window opened, and says it may not render. Feature F10-027 places a discard-all (undo) button in the title bar that appears after any change, and F10-034 describes a group header dot that discards changes. Decide one location and one visibility rule for the rebuild, and record the title bar and dot as widgets or remove them from the spec.

author: Haiku critic
text: The inventory has no clear-search control for the sidebar search field (widget 'InputWell > TextInput2'). Feature F10-011 requires an x button that appears while the query is non-empty, and F10-010 requires a blue focus outline; neither appears as a widget or state. Add the clear button and the focused-outline state to the search field entry, and state that Escape clears the query first (F10-023).

author: Haiku critic
text: The reset job is named four different ways: the row title 'Restore defaults', the button 'Reset all settings…', the confirm button 'Reset everything', and the undo tooltip 'Discard changes made since this window opened'. Pick one verb and noun for the reset control and its confirmation so the rebuilt About pane and the search terms in F10-073 match the visible label.

author: Haiku critic
text: The PathButton entry records only the non-null path and says the null state renders with no path shown, without saying what appears. Feature F10-040 requires a dash while the data folder location is loading, and the inventory has no loading state for this widget. Add the loading and null states, with their exact text, to the PathButton entry.

author: Haiku critic
text: The Data folder SettingRow, the PathButton and the Application description are tied to a local folder. The web app is cloud-based with server-side files, so there is no local data folder to open, and the description 'Tasks, attachments, screenshots and preferences' names screenshots that the web app does not have. Replace or remove the Data folder row, and rewrite the description to describe only the stored data the web app actually holds.

author: Haiku critic
text: The title bar with the three macOS traffic lights (WindowControls, MacLights, the close, minimize and full-screen Light buttons, and the draggable TitleBar) is window chrome that a browser tab does not have. Drop these widgets in the web build and keep only the 'Settings' page heading, which is the Label h1. The desktop build keeps the chrome, with its inert minimize and full-screen lights as recorded.

author: Haiku critic
text: The keyboard behaviour in feature F10-024 and F10-025 conflicts with the web rebuild. Escape closing the Settings window has no meaning in a browser page, and Command-F or Ctrl-F focusing the sidebar search would override the browser's own find shortcut, which the web build must not do. Remove these bindings from the web version and keep the search field reachable by normal focus.

author: Haiku critic
text: The window size conflicts between the sources. Feature F10-001 says the Settings window opens at a fixed 640 x 520 size, but the inventory's frame and title bar were measured at 1180 x 760 from the reference screenshot. Confirm the intended fixed size before the desktop build, and record it in the Settings window frame region, because the content pane and sidebar positions depend on it.

author: Opus (orchestrator)
text: Not in the web version: the capture bar is a desktop window summoned by a global hotkey. On the web, tasks are added by hand in the main window only.

author: Haiku critic
text: The footer-right screenshot ToolbarButton, its screenshot_monitor icon, the Capturing Spinner, the screenshot HotkeyHint and the Cmd+Shift+Enter key action all depend on screen capture, which the web version does not have. Remove them, and decide what replaces the footer-right slot (the web app uploads files to the server, so a file attach control is one option, but the inventory does not establish that). Otherwise the slot has no purpose in the web build.

author: Haiku critic
text: The inventory shows no widget for the global summon/dismiss hotkey, the click-away dismiss, or the tray entry points, yet the features list (F14-001, F14-024, F14-040 to F14-042) depends on them. The desktop rebuild needs a place in the spec for these entry points, or an explicit note that they live outside this screen.

author: Haiku critic
text: Cmd+Enter does different things depending on focus. In the notes editor it submits (submitOnModEnter), while the global capture-enter feature dismisses when the title is focused (F13-016), and plain Enter in the title saves. Pick one submit model for the same job, and state the outcome of each path in the spec.

author: Haiku critic
text: Submitting has no visible outcome in the inventory. Features F13-015 and F14-046 say submit creates the task, clears the draft and dismisses the bar, and the spec has no widget or state for success or failure feedback. Add an explicit post-submit state for both builds, since the web build has no window to dismiss.

author: Haiku critic
text: The Clear ToolbarButton, the target button and the screenshot button all carry tabIndex -1, so keyboard users cannot reach them with Tab (F13-041), and the collapsed Tab-hint button has no focus style. The web build should make these controls tabbable with a visible focus ring, since browser shortcuts take precedence and keyboard reachability is required.

author: Haiku critic
text: Two ToolbarButtons with the same size xs, well variant use different icon sizes (Clear uses iconSize 16, the screenshot button uses iconSize 15) for no stated reason. The collapsed Tab-hint button also has no hover state while the other footer and title buttons change text colour on hover. Pick one icon size and one hover rule for all ToolbarButtons.

author: Haiku critic
text: The formatting tooltips show ⌘B, ⌘I and ⌘U, and the Clear tooltip shows ⌘⇧⌫. Because browser shortcuts take precedence in the web build, Cmd+B, Cmd+I and Cmd+U may be taken by the browser, so these hints may be wrong there. The web build needs a shortcut mapping check, and the hint text should follow the shortcut that actually works.

author: Haiku critic
text: The bar is a frameless window whose height changes from 116 px to 185 px when the notes open, and it is anchored to the cursor edge (F14-015 to F14-019). The desktop build should resize a separate window and keep its anchor and screen-edge flip logic, which the inventory only describes as card heights. The web build needs none of this, since the capture bar is desktop-only.
